request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Discharge Summary:

Patient Identification:
The patient is a 67-year-old male who underwent video-assisted right lung upper lobectomy and lymph node dissection for primary lung adenocarcinoma.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the hospital in March 2012 for surgical treatment of the lung cancer. He had a history of hypertension and had been a three-packs-a-day smoker for 40 years. Blood examination on admission suggested polycythemia, which was diagnosed as smokers' polycythemia after consulting with hematologists. The appropriate phlebotomy and infusion volumes were calculated, and the patient was discharged uneventfully on postoperative day 7. The pathological diagnosis of the lung adenocarcinoma was made after the surgery.

Patient Status at Discharge:
At the time of discharge, the patient's respiratory function examination showed obstructive impairment. The serum erythropoietin level was normal, but the Hb and HCT were high. The patient was advised to continue with prescribed blood pressure medication, adhere to a healthy lifestyle, and was advised to attend regular check-ups by their physician.

Follow-up:
The patient was advised to follow up with their physician to monitor their polycythemia and lung cancer.
Primary Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]Secondary Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Procedures:
Video-assisted right lung upper lobectomy and lymph node dissection.

Allergies:
Not Applicable.

Medications:
Not Applicable.

Condition at Discharge:
Stable.

Recommendations:
The patient was advised to adhere to a healthy lifestyle and attend regular check-ups with their physician to monitor their polycythemia and lung cancer.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The episode was an admission for surgical treatment of primary lung adenocarcinoma, so the principal diagnosis is the lung cancer. The polycythemia, hypertension and smoking history are secondary. A malignant neoplasm of the upper lobe of the lung falls in C34 (malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung).

CODE: C34
